questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'The European Union' refers to.
questions.a: The European Union evolved from post-war economic cooperation through the 1957 Treaty of Rome into a political-economic union with a common currency, common foreign and security policy and member-driven institutions; the EU is the world's largest economy bloc challenges of integration remain.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The European Union'.
questions.a: The EU integrates by economics first and politics second, pooling sovereignty in trade and currency while nations keep armies.

questions.q: Under which section is 'The European Union' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: The European Union (source: leps102.txt EU evolution, institutions and currency sections)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'ASEAN's Way' refers to.
questions.a: ASEAN, founded in 1967, built regional cooperation through the 'ASEAN way' - consensus, non-interference and informality - creating an ASEAN Free Trade Area and security dialogues like the ASEAN Regional Forum without supranational institutions.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'ASEAN's Way'.
questions.a: The ASEAN way trades speed for comfort: no member is forced, so all members stay at the table.

questions.q: Under which section is 'ASEAN's Way' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: The Association of South East Asian Nations (source: leps102.txt ASEAN founding, ASEAN way and FTA sections)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'China's Rise' refers to.
questions.a: China's rise rests on the 1978 economic reforms that opened the economy to foreign investment and markets while keeping party control, producing decades of double-digit growth, the world's largest populated military modernisation and global economic weight; integration with the world economy through WTO entry deepened its rise.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'China's Rise'.
questions.a: Reform without democratisation created a distinctive model: markets in goods, party control in politics.

questions.q: Under which section is 'China's Rise' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: China (source: leps102.txt 1978 reforms, growth and WTO entry sections)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Japan and Emerging Centres' refers to.
questions.a: Japan rebuilt as an economic power after 1945 under the US security umbrella, leading in technology and aid despite constitutional limits on military role; South Korea and other Asian economies followed export-led models, adding further centres to a diversifying world economy.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Japan and Emerging Centres'.
questions.a: Economic power without matching military power defined Japan's post-war international personality.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Japan and Emerging Centres' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Japan and Korea (source: leps102.txt Japan's rise, constitution limits and Korea sections)
